info.title: Nightscout API v1
info.description:
Own your data with the Nightscout API.

This document describes API v1 as served by Nightscout 16.0.0 under `/api/v1`. `GET /versions` is served one level up, under `/api`. API v1 is also served under `/api/v2`, which adds endpoints not described here. API v3 has its own document at `/api3-docs`.

**Authentication.** A request can carry the `API_SECRET` (as its SHA-1 or SHA-512 hex digest, in the `api-secret` header), a JSON Web Token (`Authorization: Bearer <jwt>`), or an access token created in the admin tools (the `token` query parameter). The `secret` query parameter is also accepted, for existing clients. Credentials in URLs can end up in logs and browser history: see *Protecting authentication credentials in URLs* in the README. A JWT is issued for an access token by `GET /api/v2/authorization/request/{accessToken}`.

**Permissions.** Each operation below names the permission it checks, such as `api:entries:read`. A request without credentials is given the roles listed in `AUTH_DEFAULT_ROLES` (default `readable`, which grants read permissions); with `AUTH_DEFAULT_ROLES=denied` every operation that checks a permission needs credentials. A refused request is answered with HTTP 401 and `{"status":401,"message":"Unauthorized","description":"Invalid/Missing"}`.

**Availability.** Operations that change data are mounted only when `API_SECRET` is set. Writing treatments also needs `careportal` in `ENABLE`; `/alexa` and `/googlehome` need `alexa` and `googlehome` in `ENABLE`.

**Reads.** Reads of entries, treatments, devicestatus, activity and `/profiles` take a MongoDB-style filter in `find[...]` query parameters and a number of records in `count`. Without a filter on the record's date field (`date` for entries, `created_at` for treatments, devicestatus and activity, `startDate` for profiles), a read covers the last four days. Records are returned newest first.

**`count`.** `count` is a whole number of records. A value that is not (`abc`, `-3`, `1e2`) is refused with HTTP 400 `Bad count`. Two older forms are still read as 15.0.8 read them, each answered with `Deprecation: true` and a `Warning` header and each controlled by a setting described in the README: a number followed by `?` and other text is read as that number (`API_V1_COUNT_LEADING_NUMBER`), and `count=0` returns every record in a `find` that bounds one date field from both sides, or the endpoint's default number of records without such a range (`API_V1_COUNT_ZERO_WINDOW`). With a setting turned off, that form is refused, or for `count=0` answered with an empty list. A delete carrying a `count` that is not a whole number of records, `count=0` included, is refused with HTTP 400.

**Query operators.** Endpoints that accept `find[...]` support a fixed set of MongoDB query operators. On a field: `$eq` `$ne` `$gt` `$gte` `$lt` `$lte` `$in` `$nin` `$exists` `$type` `$regex` (with `$options`). At the top level of a query, or of one of their branches: `$and` `$or`. A field name with no operator is an equality match, and the indexed group form `find[$and][0][field][$op]=value` is accepted.

Any other operator is refused with HTTP 400 and a message naming it. That includes `$where`, `$function` and `$accumulator`, which ask MongoDB to run JavaScript; `$expr`, which embeds the aggregation expression language in a filter; and `$elemMatch`, `$not`, `$nor`, `$all`, `$size`, `$mod`, `$text` and the geospatial operators, none of which the API is defined over. An operator name appearing inside a *value* is data and is not affected.

**Writes.** `POST` bodies are one record or an array of at most 10000 records. Anything else is refused with HTTP 400. A write's `_id` is optional: leave it out and the server assigns one. If sent, it should be a 24-character hex string (either case), which is stored as that ObjectId in lower case. Anything else is never stored as `_id`: profile, devicestatus, food and activity refuse it with HTTP 400; treatments and entries drop it and assign one (Extended JSON `{"$oid": "<24 hex>"}` is kept as that ObjectId, and any other string is moved to `identifier` when `UUID_HANDLING` is on, the default). Reads return `_id` as the ObjectId's 24-character hex form.

tags.name: Treatments

get.description:
Returns entries, newest first. Without `count` the 10 newest are returned; without a filter on `date` or `dateString`, only entries from the last four days are considered.

The response format follows the extension (`/entries.json`, `.csv`, `.tsv`, `.txt`) or the `Accept` header. With neither, as with `Accept: */*`, the answer is tab-separated text. The text formats carry `dateString`, `date`, `sgv`, `direction` and `device` of each entry.

If `If-Modified-Since` is not before the newest entry, the answer is HTTP 304.

Permission: `api:entries:read`.

post.description:
Stores one entry or an array of entries and returns the stored records with their `_id`. A single object without a `date` is not stored and the answer is an empty array.

Permission: `api:entries:create`. Mounted only when `API_SECRET` is set.

requestBody.description: One entry or an array of entries.

delete.description:
Removes every entry matching `find`. As with `GET /entries`, without a filter on `date` or `dateString` only entries from the last four days are considered. The `count` parameter is checked but does not limit the delete.

Permission: `api:entries:delete`. Mounted only when `API_SECRET` is set.

get.description:
Returns an array holding the newest entry, of any type. Content negotiation is as for `GET /entries`.

Permission: `api:entries:read`.

post.description:
Echoes the posted entries back after the same normalisation and cleaning a `POST /entries` applies, without storing anything. Useful for checking an uploader's payload.

Permission: `api:entries:create`.

requestBody.description: One entry or an array of entries.

200.description: The entries as they would be stored.

get.summary: One entry by id, or entries of one type
get.description:
If `spec` is a 24-character hex id, returns an array holding that entry, or an empty array if no entry has that id. Otherwise `spec` is an entry type, such as `sgv`, `mbg` or `cal`, and the read is a `GET /entries` restricted to that type. A file extension selects the format, as for `GET /entries` (`/entries/sgv.json`).

Permission: `api:entries:read`.

delete.summary: Delete one entry by id, or entries of one type
delete.description:
If `spec` is a 24-character hex id, removes that entry. Otherwise `spec` is an entry type and the entries of that type matching `find` are removed; `*` matches every type.

Permission: `api:entries:delete`. Mounted only when `API_SECRET` is set.

get.summary: Records whose field matches a pattern
get.description:
Returns records from `storage` whose `field` matches a pattern built from `prefix` and `regex`. `type`, `prefix` and `regex` may be left off from the right (`/slice/entries/dateString/mbg/2015`).

`prefix` and `regex` get bash-style brace expansion, so `T{15..17}:.*` matches 3pm to 5pm. A pattern that expands to more than 2000 regular expressions is refused with HTTP 400 `Pattern too broad`. Content negotiation is as for `GET /entries`.

Permission: `api:entries:read`, and for `treatments` or `devicestatus` storage also `api:treatments:read` or `api:devicestatus:read`.

parameters.name: field
parameters.description: Name of the field the pattern is matched against, for example `dateString`.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Record type to select, for example `sgv`.

get.summary: Entries whose dateString matches a pattern
get.description:
Returns entries whose `dateString` matches a pattern built from `prefix` and `regex`, for example `/times/2015-04/T{13..18}:{00..15}` for 1pm to 6pm in April 2015. `regex`, or both parameters, may be left off. Brace expansion and its limit are as for `/slice`. Content negotiation is as for `GET /entries`.

Permission: `api:entries:read`.

get.summary: Show the query a /times request builds
get.description:
Returns the route parameters, the query and the expanded patterns that `/times/{prefix}/{regex}` would use, without reading any records. `regex`, or both parameters, may be left off.

Permission: `api:entries:read`.

200.description: The query that would be run.

get.summary: Show the query a read builds
get.description:
Returns the MongoDB query that a read of `storage` with these parameters would run, without running it. `model` is a record type such as `sgv` and may be left off; a third segment, an entry id or type, may follow it (`/echo/{storage}/{model}/{spec}`).

`storage` must name a storage layer such as `entries`, `treatments` or `devicestatus`; other names are answered with HTTP 500.

Permission: `api:entries:read`.

parameters.name: storage
parameters.description: Storage layer whose query is shown.

200.description: The query that would be run.

get.description:
Counts the records in `storage` that match `find`. The answer is an array with one object, `{"_id": null, "count": <n>}`, or an empty array when nothing matches. A `pipeline` parameter is refused with HTTP 400.

Permission: `api:entries:read`, and for `treatments` or `devicestatus` storage also `api:treatments:read` or `api:devicestatus:read`.

Returns treatments, newest `created_at` first. Without `count`, 100 treatments are returned, or 1000 when `find` is given. Without a filter on `created_at`, only treatments from the last four days are considered.

If `If-Modified-Since` is not before the newest treatment, the answer is HTTP 304.

Permission: `api:treatments:read`.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Number of treatments to return. See *count* in the description of this API.

post.description:
Stores one treatment or an array of treatments and returns them as stored, with their `_id`. A treatment without `created_at` gets the current time.

With `WRITE_VALIDATION=reject` (see the README), a Temporary Target that breaks a rule is refused: in a batch the other treatments are stored, the refused one's slot in the answer has no `_id` and a `refused` member with the reason, and a `Warning` header gives the count. A batch whose treatments are all refused, or a single refused treatment, gets HTTP 400.

Permission: `api:treatments:create`. Mounted only when `API_SECRET` is set and `careportal` is in `ENABLE`.

requestBody.description: One treatment or an array of treatments.

200.description: The stored treatments, one per treatment sent, in order.

put.description:
Stores the treatment in the body, replacing the stored treatment with the same `_id`, and returns it.

Permission: `api:treatments:update`. Mounted only when `API_SECRET` is set and `careportal` is in `ENABLE`.

delete.description:
Removes the treatments a `GET /treatments` with the same `find` would select. The `count` parameter is checked but does not limit the delete.

Permission: `api:treatments:delete`. Mounted only when `API_SECRET` is set and `careportal` is in `ENABLE`.

Removes the treatment with this `_id`, further restricted by `find` if given. `*` matches any id, so `DELETE /treatments/*` removes every treatment matching `find`.

Permission: `api:treatments:delete`. Mounted only when `API_SECRET` is set and `careportal` is in `ENABLE`.

get.description:
Returns the stored profile records, newest first. `count` sets how many (default 10). This read applies no date window.

Permission: `api:profile:read`.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Number of profile records to return (default 10).

post.description:
Stores one profile record or an array of them and returns them as stored. A record whose `_id` names a stored record replaces it, which also needs `api:profile:update`; without it the request is refused with HTTP 401 before anything is written.

Permission: `api:profile:create`. Mounted only when `API_SECRET` is set.

requestBody.description: One profile record or an array of profile records.

put.description:
Stores the profile record in the body, replacing the stored record with the same `_id`, and returns it. The body must carry a valid `_id`.

Permission: `api:profile:update`. Mounted only when `API_SECRET` is set.

delete.description:
Removes all but the newest `keep` profile records.

Permission: `api:profile:delete`. Mounted only when `API_SECRET` is set.

parameters.name: keep
parameters.description: Number of newest profile records to keep, a whole number from 10 to 10000. Other values are refused with HTTP 400.

delete.description:
Removes the profile record with this `_id`. The answer is an empty object.

Permission: `api:profile:delete`. Mounted only when `API_SECRET` is set.

get.description:
Returns the newest profile record, or `null` if there is none.

Permission: `api:profile:read`.

Returns profile records matching `find`, newest first. Without `count` 10 are returned; without a filter on `startDate`, only records whose `startDate` is in the last four days are considered.

Permission: `api:profile:read`.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Number of profile records to return (default 10). See *count* in the description of this API.

get.description:
Returns the server's status, version, enabled features and the settings clients display with. The format follows the extension or the `Accept` header: `/status.json` returns the object below, `/status.js` a script that assigns it to `this.serverSettings`, `/status.txt` and `/status.html` the text `STATUS OK`, and `/status.png` and `/status.svg` redirect to a badge image. With no extension and `Accept: */*` the answer is HTML.

When the request carries an access token, `authorized` holds a JWT issued for it (see *Authentication*); otherwise it is `null`.

Permission: `api:status:read`. Responses are sent with `Cache-Control: no-store`.

302.description: Redirect to a status badge image (`.png`, `.svg`).

get.description:
Returns devicestatus records, newest first. Without `count` 10 are returned; without a filter on `created_at`, only records from the last four days are considered.

Permission: `api:devicestatus:read`.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Number of records to return (default 10). See *count* in the description of this API.

post.description:
Stores one devicestatus record or an array of them and returns them as stored, with their `_id`.

Permission: `api:devicestatus:create`. Mounted only when `API_SECRET` is set.

requestBody.description: One devicestatus record or an array of them.

delete.summary: Delete devicestatus records matching a query
delete.description:
Removes the devicestatus records a `GET /devicestatus` with the same `find` would select.

Permission: `api:devicestatus:delete`. Mounted only when `API_SECRET` is set.

delete.summary: Delete a devicestatus record by id
delete.description:
Removes the devicestatus record with this `_id`, further restricted by `find` if given. `*` matches any id.

Permission: `api:devicestatus:delete`. Mounted only when `API_SECRET` is set.

get.description:
Returns activity records, newest first. Without a filter on `created_at`, only records from the last four days are considered.

If `If-Modified-Since` is not before the newest record, the answer is HTTP 304.

Permission: `api:activity:read`.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Number of records to return. See *count* in the description of this API.

post.description:
Stores one activity record or an array of them and returns them as stored, with their `_id`.

Permission: `api:activity:create`. Mounted only when `API_SECRET` is set.

requestBody.description: One activity record or an array of them.

put.description:
Stores the activity record in the body, replacing the stored record with the same `_id`, and returns it. The body must be one object with a valid `_id`.

Permission: `api:activity:update`. Mounted only when `API_SECRET` is set.

delete.description:
Removes the activity record with this `_id`. The answer is an empty object.

Permission: `api:activity:delete`. Mounted only when `API_SECRET` is set.

get.description:
Returns every food record, quickpicks included. This read takes no query parameters.

Permission: `api:food:read`.

post.description:
Stores one food record or an array of them and returns them as stored, with their `_id`.

Permission: `api:food:create`. Mounted only when `API_SECRET` is set.

requestBody.description: One food record or an array of them.

put.description:
Stores one food record or an array of them, each replacing the stored record with the same `_id`, and returns them as an array.

Permission: `api:food:update`. Mounted only when `API_SECRET` is set.

requestBody.description: One food record or an array of them, each with its `_id`.

delete.description:
Removes the food record with this `_id`. The answer is an empty object.

Permission: `api:food:delete`. Mounted only when `API_SECRET` is set.

get.description:
Returns the food records of type `quickpick` that are not hidden, ordered by `position`.

Permission: `api:food:read`.

Returns the food records of type `food`.

Permission: `api:food:read`.

Returns the server's messages for the administrator, such as repeated failed sign-ins. Anyone may call it: `notifyCount` is always filled in, and the messages themselves are included only for a caller with `*:*:admin`.

get.summary: Check the credentials on a request
get.description: Reports what the credentials on the request allow. Anyone may call it; a request without credentials is answered with the default roles' permissions and `message: UNAUTHORIZED`.

200.description: What the credentials allow, wrapped as `{"status": 200, "message": {...}}`.

message.description: `OK` when the credentials, not the default roles, grant `*:*:read`.

rolefound.description: `FOUND` when the credentials name a subject.

get.description:
Acknowledges, that is silences, the alarm of `level` in `group` for `time` milliseconds (30 minutes if not given). Acknowledging level 2 also acknowledges level 1. The answer is the text `OK`.

Permission: `notifications:*:ack`. Mounted only when `API_SECRET` is set. A caller without the permission is refused; the refusal is currently answered with HTTP 500 rather than 401.

parameters.name: level
parameters.description: Alarm level to acknowledge (1 warning, 2 urgent).

parameters.name: time
parameters.description: How long to silence the alarm, in milliseconds (default 30 minutes).

500.description: Refused for lack of permission (see above).

post.description: The callback Pushover calls when a user acknowledges an emergency-priority notification. It needs no credentials; the notification is identified by its `receipt`. The answer is `OK`, or HTTP 500 when no sent notification has that receipt.

400.description: The body could not be parsed.

500.description: No sent notification has this receipt.

post.description:
Answers requests from the Nightscout Alexa skill with speech built from the current data.

Permission: `api:*:read`. Mounted only when `alexa` is in `ENABLE`.

200.description: An Alexa skill response, or an empty string for a request type that takes no speech.

post.description:
Answers fulfillment requests from the Nightscout Google Home action with speech built from the current data.

Permission: `api:*:read`. Mounted only when `googlehome` is in `ENABLE`.

get.description:
Answers `{"status": "ok"}` to a caller with `authorization:debug:test`. Used to test permission checks.

Mounted only when `API_SECRET` is set.
Lists the API versions this server serves and where. Served at `/api/versions`, not under `/api/v1`. Needs no credentials.

api_secret_in_url.name: secret
api_secret_in_url.description: The same digest as `api-secret`, in the URL. Accepted for existing clients; prefer the header.

token_in_url.name: token
token_in_url.description: An access token created in the admin tools (`/admin`). Accepted for existing clients and shared links; treat such URLs as secrets.

find.name: find
find.description: Filter, in nested query syntax: `find[dateString][$gte]=2015-08-27`, `find[type]=sgv`, `find[insulin][$gte]=3`. Values arrive as strings; `date`, `sgv` and date fields are converted. See *Query operators*.

countEntries.name: count
countEntries.description: Number of entries to return (default 10). See *count* in the description of this API.

countDelete.name: count
countDelete.description: Checked like a read's `count`, but does not limit the delete. `count=0` and other values that are not a whole number of records are refused with HTTP 400.

ifModifiedSince.name: If-Modified-Since
ifModifiedSince.description: HTTP date; if the newest record returned is not newer, the answer is HTTP 304.

entrySpec.name: spec
entrySpec.description: A 24-character hex entry id, such as `55cf81bc436037528ec75fa5`, or an entry type such as `sgv`, `mbg` or `cal`.

patternPrefix.name: prefix
patternPrefix.description: Start of the pattern, matched from the beginning of the field, with brace expansion: `2015-04`, `20{14..15}-04`.

patternRegex.name: regex
patternRegex.description: Rest of the pattern, a regular expression matched anywhere after the prefix, with brace expansion: `T{13..18}:{00..15}`.

recordId.name: id
recordId.description: The record's `_id`, a 24-character hex string. Other values are refused with HTTP 400.

Entries.description: An array of entries. JSON, or text in the format the extension or `Accept` header asks for.

BadRequest.description: The request was refused: a malformed `count`, a refused query operator, a malformed body or `_id`, or too many records.

Unauthorized.description: The credentials, or the default roles, do not grant the permission.
